parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: A balanced HAZOP assessment of Node 1 was performed across all defined parameters (Pressure, Level, Flow, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures). To prevent availability bias induced by the training vignette detailing depressurization, equal scrutiny was given to overpressurization, liquid carryover, gas blowby, and documented human-procedural start-up deviations.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Reverse Flow: No specific check valves, backflow configurations, or high-pressure downstream cross-connections are documented in Node 1 packet.
Fire/Explosion (External): External pool fire or ambient explosion scenarios are unresolved due to lack of fireproofing, deluge, and spacing data in the system packet.
Another / Contaminant: Chemical contamination or foreign fluid ingress is unresolved due to absence of upstream additive or chemical injection specifications.

consequences: Overpressurization of FWKO drum V-001 beyond design rating (published operating range 125 psig, nominal 60 psig)
Potential loss of containment or flaring upset

evidence.relevance: Provides nominal pressure (60 psig) and published operating limits (125 psig).
Identifies pressure control PV-101, pressure transmitter PIT-101, and safety relief valves PSV-101 A/B.

possible_causes: Blockage or backpressure in the fuel gas header or burn pit line
recommendations: Verify PSV-101 A/B sizing and setpoints against vessel design pressure and maximum operating pressure of 125 psig.
Ensure PIT-101 is configured to trip inlet isolation SDV-30010 on high-high pressure.

consequences: Depressurization of V-001 below nominal 60 psig
Disruption of separated fuel gas supply to downstream users
Potential process instability in downstream Heater-Treater

evidence.relevance: Specifies nominal operating pressure of 60 psig.
Describes routing of separated gas to fuel gas and burn pit.
Documents PV-101 and PIT-101 in Node 1.

possible_causes: Excessive gas routing to fuel gas system or burn pit
recommendations: Evaluate low-pressure trip/alarm logic on PIT-101 to restrict fuel gas off-take upon low separator pressure.

consequences: Liquid carryover into the gas line to fuel gas consumers or burn pit
Potential flaring hazard or engine/generator liquid slugging

evidence.relevance: Defines disposition of gas, oil, and water streams.
Lists level valves LV-101, LV-102, and safety shutdown valves SDV-101, SDV-102.

possible_causes: Level control valves LV-101 (oil) or LV-102 (water) fail closed
Downstream blockage in oil transfer to Heater-Treater or water transfer to water treatment
recommendations: Confirm high-high liquid level interlock initiates closure of inlet SDV-30010 to prevent gas line liquid overflow.

consequences: Gas blowby into oily line to Heater-Treater or water line to water treatment
Overpressurization or upset of downstream low-pressure separation equipment
existing_safeguards: LV-101 and LV-102 level control loops
possible_causes: Spurious opening of level control valves
recommendations: Confirm low-low liquid level trip closes SDV-101 and SDV-102 to isolate outlets and prevent downstream gas blowby.

consequences: Starvation of downstream Heater-Treater and V-003 Electrostatic Desalter

evidence.relevance: Maps process flow from V-001 through desalter.

possible_causes: Inadvertent closure of inlet valve SDV-30010
Upstream line blockage or field supply disruption
recommendations: Ensure operational response procedures exist for FAL-103 alarm to verify upstream valve lineup and protect downstream equipment.

consequences: Operating temperature deviation outside the 130 °F nominal to 200 °F envelope
Degraded three-phase oil-water separation efficiency in V-001

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal temperature (130 °F) and upper limit (200 °F).
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger within Node 1.

existing_safeguards: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger process controls
possible_causes: Malfunction or thermal duty upset in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Review E-001 thermal control limits and temperature monitoring safeguards upstream of V-001.

consequences: Pressure/flow surge into V-001 FWKO drum on start-up
Improper three-phase separation and potential carryover/blowby during transient start-up

evidence.relevance: Includes Start/Stop Procedures as a required study element.
Specifies known start-up procedural vulnerability concerning FWKO bypass opening.

possible_causes: Operator error or checklist omission during FWKO start-up
Failure to open FWKO bypass line prior to start-up
recommendations: Update the pre-startup operating checklist to make FWKO bypass verification a mandatory sign-off step before admitting crude feed.

consequences: Wall loss and integrity degradation in V-001 or water/oil draw piping

evidence.relevance: Identifies separation of free water and crude oil.
Lists Corrosion/Erosion as a required Node 1 HAZOP element.

possible_causes: Corrosive constituents in produced water and crude oil
Sand or particulate erosion in bottom liquid zones and lines
recommendations: Establish an ultrasonic thickness (UT) inspection program and corrosion coupon monitoring for V-001 shell and bottom water draw lines.

uncertainty_notes: Specific interlock logic linking PIT-101 and FAL-103 to emergency shutdown valves (SDV-30010, SDV-101, SDV-102) is not explicitly detailed in the packet.
Corrosion monitoring provisions, metallurgy, and inspection records for V-001 are not documented in the system packet.
Specific operating envelopes and trip setpoints for E-001 are omitted beyond the general temperature range.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWPRESSURE-01__salient_history__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Background training vignette
Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A pressure-control loop failed open and the separator depressurized; generators stopped and the unit shut down. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

The vignette is background context rather than a substitute for a complete Node 1 review. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
